meta.title: English Future Continuous Tenses Test
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Future Continuous Tenses themed around mobile games, combining at least one or more grammar topics per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Future Continuous tense paired with topics like conditionals, gerunds, relative clauses, passive voice, quantifiers, and more, all within familiar mobile gaming contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: When the new gacha banner drops tomorrow, I _____ my last few gems, hoping I _____ the limited character.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with a time clause and a Future Simple tense. 'Will be spending' describes an action in progress at a specific future time, while 'will pull' expresses a future hope or prediction.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous for actions in progress at a specific future time
explanation.formula: When + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing, hoping + subject + will + base verb
examples: When the update launches, I will be downloading it immediately.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle 'grinding'. The verbs 'avoid' and the preposition context require the gerund 'playing', not the to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Present participle after 'will be' and gerunds after specific verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing; avoid + verb-ing
examples: I will be studying later, so I am avoiding playing games.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the tournament starts, _____ of the top players will be warming up, while _____ of the audience will be streaming the event.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with quantifiers. 'Players' is a countable plural noun, requiring 'many'. 'Audience' (referring to the collective mass of people or viewership) is treated as an uncountable concept here, requiring 'much', or 'much of the audience'.
explanation.concept: Countable vs. uncountable quantifiers with Future Continuous
explanation.formula: Many of + plural countable noun + will be + verb-ing; much of + uncountable noun + will be + verb-ing
examples: Many of the users will be logging in, while much of the traffic will be routing through the main server.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with relative clauses and subject-verb agreement. 'Members' is plural, requiring 'who are'. 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle 'expecting'. 'A lot of' is the correct quantifier phrase.
explanation.topic: Future Continuous + Relative Clauses + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Plural agreement in relative clauses and correct participle formation
explanation.formula: Plural noun + who + are + verb-ing + will be + verb-ing + a lot of + plural noun
examples: The players who are queuing will be expecting a lot of rewards.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: If the servers do not crash during the launch, millions of players _____ the new battle royale map at the same time.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with a First Conditional structure. The Future Continuous ('will be exploring') emphasizes an action that will be in progress at a specific future time if the condition is met.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous in the main clause of a first conditional
explanation.formula: If + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: If it rains, we will be staying indoors all day.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with phrasal verbs. 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle 'scouting' to form the continuous aspect of the phrasal verb 'scout out'.
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect of separable and inseparable phrasal verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing + particle + object
examples: I will be setting up the router while you will be logging in.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The pro player, whose mechanics _____ the community for years, _____ in the grand finals this weekend.

A.text: will be amazing / will be competing

B.text: has been amazing / will be competing

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with a non-defining relative clause in the Present Perfect Continuous. 'Has been amazing' describes an ongoing past-to-present action, while 'will be competing' describes a future arrangement.
explanation.concept: Combining Present Perfect Continuous in relative clauses with Future Continuous in the main clause
explanation.formula: Noun, whose + subject + has been + verb-ing, + will be + verb-ing
examples: The developer, who has been working tirelessly, will be presenting the demo.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before words starting with a /j/ sound
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: They will be building a unique experience.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Don't call me at 9 PM; I _____ the daily quests, and my phone _____ on Do Not Disturb mode.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with modal-like future expressions. 'Will be doing' emphasizes an action in progress at a specific future time, and 'will be' describes the future state of the phone.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous for actions in progress and Future Simple for states
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing; subject + will be + adjective/noun
examples: I will be sleeping, and my phone will be off.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with adverb placement. When using 'always' to express annoyance or emphasis in continuous tenses, it must be placed between the modal 'will' and the auxiliary 'be' ('will always be fixing').
explanation.concept: Correct placement of frequency adverbs in Future Continuous
explanation.formula: Subject + will + always + be + verb-ing
examples: He will always be complaining about the meta.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: While the developers _____ the new patch notes, the community _____ theories about the hidden changes.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with conjunctions of time. 'While' + Present Continuous sets the background future action, and the main clause uses Future Continuous for a simultaneous ongoing action.
explanation.concept: Parallel actions in progress at a specific future time
explanation.formula: While + subject + present continuous, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: While I am cooking dinner, you will be setting the table.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with preposition collocations. 'Relying' is always followed by 'on', and 'accustomed' is followed by 'to'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific verbs and adjectives
explanation.formula: Will be + relying on + noun; am accustomed to + verb-ing
examples: I will be relying on you, and I am accustomed to working late.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the elliptical sentence.
data.question: My brother will be grinding the new raid tonight, and I _____ tomorrow.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with ellipsis. The auxiliary 'will be' is used to avoid repeating the full verb phrase ('will be grinding the new raid').
explanation.concept: Omitting repeated verb phrases using auxiliary verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing + object, and + subject + will be
examples: She will be traveling next week, and I will be too.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with discourse markers. 'However' is required to show the contrast between the maintenance and the ability to access offline mode, rather than 'therefore' (which shows result).
explanation.concept: Using contrastive discourse markers with Future Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing; however, + subject + will be + able to + verb
examples: The server will be down; however, we will be testing locally.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: As the meta evolves, the top-tier characters _____ more complex, and players _____ adapting their strategies accordingly.

B.text: will be becoming / will be adapting

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with advanced comparatives and conjunctions of time. 'Will be becoming' and 'will be adapting' emphasize ongoing, changing situations in the future.
explanation.concept: Describing changing situations and trends with 'as' using Future Continuous
explanation.formula: As + subject + verb + s/es, subject + will be + becoming + more + adjective, and + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: As the game grows, the mechanics will be becoming more intricate.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with cleft sentences for emphasis. 'It will be' is required to emphasize the future subject, matching the Future Continuous 'will be addressing' in the relative clause.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement and future tense in it-cleft structures
explanation.formula: It + will be + plural noun + who + will be + verb-ing
examples: It will be the developers who will be explaining the changes.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: What excites me most is that, during the anniversary event, the developers _____ exclusive cosmetics to all active players.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with noun clauses. 'Will be giving away' emphasizes an action that will be in progress or planned as part of a future arrangement during the event.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous in noun clauses to describe planned future actions
explanation.formula: What + present simple + is that + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: What I know is that they will be releasing a teaser soon.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with verb patterns. The phrasal verb 'plan on' must be followed by a gerund ('participating'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Gerunds required after specific phrasal verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + planning on + verb-ing; subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: We are planning on joining, so we will be grinding ranks.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Even though the new update _____ bugs at launch, the community will be supporting the developers through the patching process.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with adverbial clauses of concession. In concession clauses referring to the future, the Present Simple ('has') is used, while the main clause uses Future Continuous.
explanation.topic: Future Continuous + Adverbial Clauses of Concession
explanation.concept: Using Present Simple for future meaning in concessive clauses
explanation.formula: Even though + subject + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: Even though it rains, we will be playing outside.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: Wait, 'having to' is correct. Let's make an error: 'will be have to'.
This combines the Future Continuous tense with perfect infinitives/modal-like structures. 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle 'having' to form the continuous aspect of 'have to'.
explanation.topic: Future Continuous + Perfect Infinitives / Modal-like structures
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect of semi-modals
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + having to + base verb
examples: I will be having to explain this repeatedly.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the energy cap resets, I _____ my daily tasks, but my friend _____ still farming for materials.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the Future Continuous tense. 'Will have finished' describes an action completed before a future time, while 'will be farming' describes an action in progress at that same future time.
explanation.concept: Contrasting completed future actions with ongoing future actions
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have + past participle, but + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: By 5 PM, I will have left, but she will be working.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. The phrasal verb 'look forward to' uses 'to' as a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund ('seeing'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Gerunds required after prepositional phrasal verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + looking forward to + verb-ing; subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: I am looking forward to meeting you, and I will be waiting at the lobby.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Since I am used to _____ auto-battle features, I _____ relying on them during the upcoming grind.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with the 'be used to' structure. 'Be used to' is followed by a gerund ('using'), and the main clause uses Future Continuous ('will be relying') for a future ongoing action.
explanation.concept: Gerunds after 'be used to' and Future Continuous for future habits
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + used to + verb-ing; subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: I am used to waking up early, so I will be studying at dawn.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'not only... but also' inversion. When 'not only' begins a clause, it triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('will the team be competing').
explanation.topic: Future Continuous + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'not only' in Future Continuous
explanation.formula: Not only + will + subject + be + verb-ing, but + subject + will + also + be + verb-ing
examples: Not only will she be singing, but she will also be dancing.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: As soon as the maintenance ends, thousands of players _____ in, and the servers _____ under heavy load.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'as soon as' time clauses. 'Will be logging' emphasizes the massive, ongoing action happening immediately after the future event, and 'will be' describes the resulting future state.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous for immediate, ongoing future actions after a time marker
explanation.formula: As soon as + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing, and + subject + will be + adjective
examples: As soon as the bell rings, the students will be rushing out.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'so... that' structures. 'So' is used with adjectives ('high'), while 'such' is used with nouns. The Future Continuous 'will be unplayable' describes the future state resulting from the condition.
explanation.concept: Using 'so' with adjectives in Future Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + so + adjective + that + subject + will be + adjective
examples: The traffic will be so bad that we will be late.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Unless the developers _____ the matchmaking algorithm, casual players _____ matched against max-level opponents.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'unless' conditional clauses. 'Unless' takes the Present Simple ('fix'), and the main clause uses Future Continuous ('will be matched' - passive, or 'will be facing' - active. Let's use 'will be facing' for active Future Continuous). Wait, the option says 'will be'. Let's adjust the question to active voice: 'casual players will be facing max-level opponents'.
explanation.question: Unless the developers _____ the matchmaking algorithm, casual players _____ max-level opponents.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'unless' conditional clauses. 'Unless' takes the Present Simple ('fix'), and the main clause uses Future Continuous ('will be facing') to describe an ongoing future situation.
explanation.concept: Using Present Simple in 'unless' clauses and Future Continuous in the main clause
explanation.formula: Unless + subject + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: Unless you hurry, you will be missing the bus.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: Wait, I need an error. Let's make it: 'either the tank will be initiate'.

This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'either... or' correlative conjunctions. 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle 'initiating' to maintain parallel Future Continuous structure.
explanation.concept: Maintaining parallel Future Continuous structure with correlative conjunctions
explanation.formula: Either + subject + will be + verb-ing, or + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: Either I will be cooking, or she will be ordering.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I don't know whether the new character _____ overpowered or not, but the community _____ discussing it for weeks.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'whether... or not' noun clauses. 'Will be' describes a future state, and 'will be discussing' emphasizes an ongoing future action.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous in 'whether' clauses and main clauses
explanation.formula: Subject + present simple + whether + subject + will be + adjective, but + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: I wonder whether it will be raining, but we will be going anyway.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'in order to' infinitive phrases of purpose. 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle 'spending' to form the Future Continuous tense.
explanation.concept: Future Continuous for planned actions following a purpose clause
explanation.formula: In order to + base verb, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: In order to pass, I will be studying all night.
